items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I got a gig, Jenkins got a gig for me, he couldn't make it and he loaned me his horn.

ctx.x: And the show opened with a bang. We played dinner engagements and nightclub engagements, we used to work from 6:00 to 8:00, from 10:00 to 2:00. The band was a riot, the show was great. We played right on through 1929 into 1930. Two weeks after 1930, business started falling off. You know the crash came in 1929, and so it was gradually, the times were catching up with the crash. So in about another week and a half I used to go to work by streetcar, because streetcar would put me off a block from where I worked and…

on the streetcar in front of my house. So this particular day I went down to go to work, and I walked in and there had been a fire. And I saw my beautiful saxophone all curled up where it was burned up. All the instruments were burned up. So that meant that Trent's band were locked in Cleveland, Ohio without instruments. So, we were exploited by two or three groups, they gave benefit dances for us, and we --when the dance was all over, when you checked to see how much money you had in the pot, you had none. So…

And we stayed in Cleveland that whole winter. Finally Alphonso Trent's father got together and took us out to the King Factory in Cleveland, Ohio, and they bought everybody an instrument. His father, his people put up the money and got everybody in the band an instrument. Now Spring of 1930. We started a tour and we booked into Columbus, Ohio, and we get to Columbus, Ohio and there was another band booked in there, Sammy Stewart's orchestra and that was Sammy Stewart's home, he was a Chicago band, and his band…
